items.title: Scriptural Authority Opens: The Third Source of Valid Knowledge

items.zh: 正教量者，謂一切智所說言教，或從彼聞，或隨彼法。
items.en: Scriptural authority: it refers to the teaching spoken by the all-knowing one, or what is heard directly from him, or what accords with his teaching.

items.zh: 此復三種。一、不違聖言，二、能治雜染，三、不違法相。不違聖言者，謂聖弟子說，或佛自說經教，展轉流布至今，不違正法、不違正義。能治雜染者，謂隨此法善修習時，能永調伏貪瞋癡等一切煩惱及隨煩惱。不違法相者，謂翻違法相，當知即是不違法相。
items.en: This again has three kinds: first, not contradicting the sacred word; second, capable of curing defilement; and third, not contradicting the nature of things. Not contradicting the sacred word: whether spoken by a noble disciple or by the Buddha himself, and transmitted down to the present, it does not contradict the true Dharma or its true meaning. Capable of curing defilement: when this teaching is well practised, it is capable of permanently subduing craving, aversion, delusion, and all other afflictions and secondary afflictions. Not contradicting the nature of things: its character should be known as the reverse of contradicting the nature of things.

items.title: Six Ways to Misrepresent Reality — And the Basis of Discourse Completes

items.zh: 何等名為違法相耶？謂於無相，增為有相。如執有我、有情、命者、生者等類；或常、或斷，有色、無色，如是等類。或於有相，減為無相。
items.en: What is called contradicting the nature of things? It means, regarding what has no real mark, augmenting it into having one — as in holding there to be a self, a sentient being, a life, a born one, and so on; or holding it permanent, or annihilated, possessing form, or formless, and so on. Or, regarding what has a real mark, diminishing it into having none.

items.zh: 或於決定，立為不定。如一切行皆是無常，一切有漏皆性是苦，一切諸法皆空無我，而妄建立一分是常，一分無常；一分是苦，一分非苦；一分有我，一分無我。於佛所立不可記法，尋求記別，謂為可記，或安立記。或於不定，建立為定。
items.en: Or, regarding what is fixed, positing it as unfixed — as with all conditioned things being impermanent, all that is defiled being of the nature of suffering, all things being empty and without self, one falsely holds that some part is permanent and some part impermanent... Or, seeking to pronounce upon matters the Buddha established as beyond pronouncement, holding them pronounceable, or actually pronouncing upon them. Or, regarding what is unfixed, positing it as fixed.

items.zh: 如執一切樂受皆貪所隨眠，一切苦受瞋所隨眠，一切不苦不樂受癡所隨眠，一切樂受皆是有漏，一切樂俱故思造業一向決定受苦異熟，如是等類。
或於有相法中，無差別相，建立差別；有差別相，立無差別。如於有為無差別相，於無為中亦復建立；於無為法無差別相，於有為法亦復建立。如於有為無為，如是於有色無色、有見無見、有對無對、有漏無漏，隨其所應皆當了知。又於有相，不如正理立因果相。如立妙行感不愛果，立諸惡行感可愛果；
items.en: Or, within things that have marks, positing differentiation where there is none, or positing no differentiation where there is. And, regarding things with marks, positing the relation of cause and effect contrary to correct principle — as positing that wholesome conduct brings an undesirable result, and unwholesome conduct brings a desirable one.

items.zh: 計惡說法毘奈耶中，習諸邪行，能得清淨；於善說法毘奈耶中，修行正行，謂為雜染。於不實相，以假言說立真實相；於真實相，以假言說種種安立。如於一切離言法中，建立言說，說第一義。如是等類，名違法相。與此相違，當知即是不違法相。是名正教。
items.en: Holding that practising wrong conduct within a wrongly taught doctrine and discipline yields purity, while practising right conduct within a well-taught doctrine and discipline yields defilement. Establishing a merely provisional designation as the true mark of what is not truly marked; and, regarding what is truly marked, elaborating it through various provisional designations. Things of this kind are called contradicting the nature of things. The reverse of this should be known as not contradicting the nature of things. This is called scriptural authority.

items.title: Closing Questions: Why Each Piece Comes in Its Order — The Basis of Discourse Concludes

items.zh: 問：若一切法自相成就，各自安立己法性中，復何因緣建立二種所成義耶？答：為欲令他生信解故，非為生成諸法性相。
items.en: Question: if all things are already established in their own nature, each abiding in its own inherent character, then for what reason does one establish the two kinds of meaning to be established? Answer: it is in order to generate confidence and understanding in others — not in order to generate the nature or mark of things themselves.

items.zh: 問：為欲成就所成立義，何故先立宗耶？答：為先顯示自所愛樂宗義故。問：何故次辯因耶？答：為欲開顯依現見事決定道理，令他攝受所立宗義故。問：何故次引喻耶？答：為欲顯示能成道理之所依止現見事故。
items.en: Question: in order to accomplish the meaning to be established, why does one posit the thesis first? Answer: in order first to display the thesis one cherishes oneself. Question: why does one next distinguish the reason? Answer: in order to unfold, resting on directly observed fact, a settled principle, so as to bring another to accept the thesis posited. Question: why does one next cite the example? Answer: in order to display the directly observed fact on which the reasoning's principle itself depends.

items.zh: 問：何故後說同類、異類、現量、比量、正教等耶？答：為欲開示因喻二種相違、不相違智故。又相違者，由二因緣。一、不決定故；二、同所成故。不相違者，亦二因緣。一、決定故；二、異所成故。其相違者，於為成就所立宗義，不能為量，故不名量。不相違者，於為成就所立宗義，能為正量，故名為量。
items.en: Question: why does one then speak of the similar class, the dissimilar class, direct perception, inference, and scriptural authority? Answer: it is in order to reveal the knowledge of whether the reason and example are, or are not, in conflict with the thesis. Being in conflict comes from two causes: first, being indeterminate; second, being, like the thesis itself, still in need of establishment. Not being in conflict likewise comes from two causes: first, being determinate; second, not being, like the thesis, still in need of establishment. What is in conflict... cannot serve as valid knowledge, and so is not called valid knowledge. What is not in conflict... can serve as genuinely valid knowledge, and so is called valid knowledge.
This is called the basis of discourse.

blocks.text: The third means of valid knowledge is **scriptural authority** (正教量, *āgama*): trustworthy teaching. The treatise explains what makes a teaching trustworthy, and then lists six ways teachings misrepresent reality. One of them is the "wrong grasp of emptiness" we met on Day 50.

A teaching is trustworthy if it does not contradict the scriptures, if it cures defilement, and if it does not contradict the nature of things. Master Cháng Bǎi on the second criterion: affliction is singled out because "it causes all the suffering of birth and death; with affliction there is karma, with karma, suffering." A teaching that does not reduce affliction is not the Buddha's, whatever its source.

Someone objects: teachings passed by word of mouth are distorted, like a whispered message passed along a line. Venerable Miào Jìng answers: "The Buddhadharma can't be described that way, because when the Buddha taught, the first hearers were noble disciples who had attained the path." Master Cháng Bǎi distinguishes "learned noble disciples" (ordinary beings who have studied) from plain "noble disciples" (those who have seen the truths). The tradition was carried first by people who had verified it.

Teachings go wrong in six ways, in pairs: superimposing what does not exist; denying what does; positing the fixed as unfixed; the unfixed as fixed; the unpronounceable as pronounceable; and the reverse.

"**Diminishing what has a real mark into having none**": Master Cháng Bǎi's example is the wrong grasp of emptiness. "Emptiness means that dependent arising lacks self-nature; it does not deny dependent arising" (Days 50, 89). This is the Yogācāra criticism in a sentence.
Another error is holding that all pleasant feeling is bound to craving. Master Cháng Bǎi: not all pleasure is contaminated; noble ones have joy and pleasure too, uncontaminated.

Closing questions explain why the elements of a debate come in their order: thesis, reason, example, and so on. If everything is already what it is, why establish a thesis at all? To generate understanding in others. Master Cháng Bǎi: "Though one who has reached the shore needs no boat, before reaching it one must still board the boat." Logic, like scripture, is a raft.

The reason must "unfold a settled principle resting on observed fact": Venerable Miào Jìng: "a principle you agree with and I agree with". A reason the opponent does not accept proves nothing. The *Pīxún jì* names this fault: a reason that itself still needs proof.

quiz.q: Someone objects that oral transmission distorts like a game of telephone. How does Venerable Miào Jìng reply, and what does the note say?
options: the Dharma is different: its first transmitters were noble disciples who had attained the path; the note says fidelity to source matters, not attainment
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The Buddhadharma can't be described that way, because when the Buddha taught, the first recipients were all noble disciples who had attained the path." What ordinary people say must be checked against the Buddha's word.

quiz.q: The Pixunji distinguishes "learned noble disciples" from "noble disciples." Which section is cited, and what does the note say?
options: the 攝事分, fascicle 94 — "learned" marks ordinary beings, plain "noble disciple" one who has seen the truths; the note misnames it the Compendium of Determinations
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: if a sutra says only "noble disciples" without "learned," it means they have seen the four truths — citing the 攝事分, fascicle 94. The note's "Compendium of Determinations" is wrong.

quiz.q: Why does the second criterion, "curing defilement," single out affliction, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: affliction is the cause of all suffering in birth and death: affliction leads to karma, karma to suffering
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: affliction is singled out because it causes all the suffering of birth and death — with affliction one creates karma, and karma yields suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng: cutting affliction is the root of all merit.

quiz.q: "Diminishing what has a real mark into having none" — how does Master Cháng Bǎi illustrate this error?
options: the wrong grasp of emptiness — emptiness means dependent arising lacks self-nature, not denying dependent arising; it is empty in its very being
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: emptiness because dependent arising lacks self-nature does not deny dependent arising; dependent arising itself is empty. Holding ultimate emptiness while ignoring that it never departs from dependent existence is diminution.

quiz.q: If all things are already established in their nature, why establish a thesis? To generate others' confidence. What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: once ashore one needs no boat, but before arriving one must board it — the boat carries one to nirvāṇa's shore
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Though one who has reached the shore needs no boat, before reaching it one must still board; the boat carries one to the far shore of nirvāṇa, so it can't be dispensed with." Venerable Miào Jìng: reasoning doesn't create the nature of things.

quiz.q: The reason "unfolds a settled principle resting on observed fact." How does Venerable Miào Jìng define a "settled principle"?
options: a principle both you and I accept — once stated, both sides agree; that is settled
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "A principle you agree with and I agree with — once stated, you agree and I agree; that principle is settled." The example displays the observed fact on which the reasoning rests.

quiz.q: The second cause of conflict, 同所成, is rendered "merely restating what was to be established." How do the lectures read it?
options: the reason and example are not mutually accepted and still need proof themselves — the reason is unestablished, not a restatement of the thesis
quiz.why: The *Pixunji*: if the reason and example are not mutually accepted and still await proof, they cannot establish anything — this is 同所成. Venerable Miào Jìng: you give a reason, yet it's as if you said nothing.
